**(i)** Events $A$ and $B$ are such that $P(A) = \frac{1}{3}$, $P(B) = \frac{2}{5}$ and $P(A/B) = \frac{1}{4}$.

Calculate

questions.corrige_markdown:
**Law used:** the multiplication law, $P(A \cap B) = P(A/B) \times P(B)$.

$$P(A \cap B) = \frac{1}{4} \times \frac{2}{5} = \frac{2}{20} = \frac{1}{10}$$

**$P(A \cap B) = \dfrac{1}{10}$.**

**Law used:** the addition law, $P(A \cup B) = P(A) + P(B) - P(A \cap B)$.

$$P(A \cup B) = \frac{1}{3} + \frac{2}{5} - \frac{1}{10} = \frac{10 + 12 - 3}{30} = \frac{19}{30}$$

**$P(A \cup B) = \dfrac{19}{30}$** ($\approx 0.633$).

By definition of conditional probability, $P(B/A^c) = \dfrac{P(B \cap A^c)}{P(A^c)}$.

- $P(A^c) = 1 - P(A) = 1 - \dfrac{1}{3} = \dfrac{2}{3}$.
- $B$ is the union of the disjoint events $B \cap A$ and $B \cap A^c$, so $P(B \cap A^c) = P(B) - P(A \cap B) = \dfrac{2}{5} - \dfrac{1}{10} = \dfrac{3}{10}$.

$$P(B/A^c) = \frac{3/10}{2/3} = \frac{3}{10} \times \frac{3}{2} = \frac{9}{20}$$

**$P(B/A^c) = \dfrac{9}{20} = 0.45$.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
**(ii)** An animal feed store stocks feed for pigs and fowls in bags. 30% of the stock is pig feed and 70% is fowl feed. 5% of the pig feed and 10% of the fowl feed are known to have expired.

A bag of animal feed is taken out from the store at random.

(a) Sketch a tree diagram to show all possible outcomes and their respective probabilities.
questions.corrige_markdown:
Let $P$ = "the bag is pig feed", $F$ = "the bag is fowl feed", $E$ = "the bag has expired". The first set of branches gives the type of feed, the second set gives whether it has expired (the second probabilities are conditional on the type).

```
                      0.05 ---- Expired        P and E     : 0.3 x 0.05 = 0.015
          0.3  Pig  <
        /             0.95 ---- Not expired    P and E'    : 0.3 x 0.95 = 0.285
 Start <
        \             0.10 ---- Expired        F and E     : 0.7 x 0.10 = 0.070
          0.7  Fowl <
                      0.90 ---- Not expired    F and E'    : 0.7 x 0.90 = 0.630
```

| Outcome | Probability |
|---|---|
| Pig feed, expired | $0.3 \times 0.05 = 0.015$ |
| Pig feed, not expired | $0.3 \times 0.95 = 0.285$ |
| Fowl feed, expired | $0.7 \times 0.10 = 0.070$ |
| Fowl feed, not expired | $0.7 \times 0.90 = 0.630$ |

Check: the four outcome probabilities add up to $0.015 + 0.285 + 0.070 + 0.630 = 1$. On the sketch: the two first branches carry $0.3$ and $0.7$ (sum 1), and each pair of second branches sums to 1.

questions.enonce_markdown: (b) Find the probability that the bag of feed has expired.
questions.corrige_markdown:
A bag has expired in exactly two (mutually exclusive) ways: it is pig feed and expired, or it is fowl feed and expired. Adding the two branch products of the tree (total probability law):

$$P(E) = P(P) \times P(E/P) + P(F) \times P(E/F) = 0.3 \times 0.05 + 0.7 \times 0.10 = 0.015 + 0.070 = 0.085$$

**$P(\text{bag has expired}) = 0.085$** ($= \dfrac{17}{200}$).
